files.desc: Horsley, Britannia Romana (1732), P.44 (leaf n0114): the two legionary camps of the Mons Graupius campaign per the book's text pp.43-44 ('the legions might poflibly have been at Ardoch, or Innerpeffery, before they marched to the battle'): Ardoch camp (the lower plan, concentric with a Praetorium box, the Knoch river on its west and the Ruchel to its north) and the Innerpeffery camp (the upper plan, a single circuit with a military way and 'a bank by which the river has formerly run'; each plan with its 200-yard scale). The Ardoch row is the Braco camp (Q4788225, Gask Ridge - DECISIONS 808 148); the Innerpeffery camp is recorded here on this row (the 808 box: no row of its own). Internet Archive britanniaromanao00hors, leaf n0114 of the 936-leaf Google scan (British Museum volume).
files.name: The legionary camps of Ardoch and Innerpeffery, two plans, Horsley (1732), P.44
files.title: Innerpeffery camp. and Ardoch camp.

files.desc: Horsley, Britannia Romana (1732), P.113 (leaf n0185): five fort plans - I GLANNIBANTA (Lanchester), II ALIONE (Whitley castle), III BREMETEN RACUM (Old Penrith), IV OLENACUM (Old Carlisle), V VIROSIDUM (near Elenborough), with Praetorium boxes on I and III, Watling Street, a compass and 'A feale of 100 paces'. I-IV have catalog rows (longovicium-q6674222, whitley-castle-q7996561, voreda-roman-fort-q17642742, luguvallium-q71551754); the row ties to V VIROSIDUM, the only one of the five without a catalog row, as the plate's new no-QID 'roman fort' row - all five plans are equal, so no other ranking (DECISIONS 808 147 item 4). Internet Archive britanniaromanao00hors, leaf n0185 of the 936-leaf Google scan (British Museum volume).

files.desc: Horsley, Britannia Romana (1732), P.158 N.1 (leaf n0236): a general map of the Roman walls in the north of England and so much of the adjacent countryes as includes the secondary stations per lineam valli: the whole line from Segedunum (SEGEDYNVM) to Tunnocelum (TIVN NOCELVM), every station labelled (B's read: PONSAELII, CONDERCVVM, VINDOBALA, HYNVNVM, CILVRNVM, BORCOVICVS, PROCOLITIA, MAGNA, PETRIANA, AESTICA, VINDOLANA, ALIONE, GLANNIBANTA, BREMENIVM, BREMETERACVM, BROCAVVM, BRONONACAE, BLATVM VVLGIVM, CASTRA EXPLORATORVM, CORSTOPITVM, GALLAVA, HABITANCVM, VINDOMORA, ABALLABA, AMBBOGLANNA, CONGAVATA, AXELODYNYVM, LVGVAVALLIVM, OLENACVM, VIROSIDVM, GABROSENTVM; a scale of ten miles) - no inset fort plans: the map itself is the series' subject, so the row ties to the wall's east end, Segedunum (DECISIONS 808 147 item 6). Internet Archive britanniaromanao00hors, leaf n0236 of the 936-leaf Google scan (British Museum volume).

files.desc: Horsley, Britannia Romana (1732), P.176 N.1 (leaf n0278): a general map of Antoninus's wall in Scotland: the whole wall line from the west end to Falkirk, with the forts and camps named (B's read: New Kirkpatrick, Old Kirkpatrick, Duntocher, Castle-hill, Bemulie, Kirkintilloch, Auchindavy, Barhill, Crowyhill, Wellerwood, Castle-cary, Rough-castle, Camelon, Falkirk, Mumrills, Caer-niden, Abercorn, Alaterva, Glasgow, Hamilton, Edinburgh, Leviston, Lindthgow, Reafew, the Calder, Alordur, Gartnavan, Dangoin hill; a scale of ten miles). Tied to the wall's west end, Bar Hill (the reused bar-hill-fort row - DECISIONS 808 147 item 6). Internet Archive britanniaromanao00hors, leaf n0278 of the 936-leaf Google scan (British Museum volume).
